report: One-month pruritic, painful periorbital eruption with scaly crusted pink plaques in a woman in her 70s; left eyelid biopsy shows vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy, and both pathologist and laboratory physician favor a lupus-related process. Her lupus nephritis and immune thrombocytopenia support autoimmunity. Infection, neoplasm and drug eruption are unlikely; dermatomyositis, lichen planus and GVHD lack support. Missing DIF and serology limit certainty.
